title: Count of Sabugosa to Queen Amélie, four code telegrams of 1903, 1904 and 1910 (ANTT PT/TT/CAM/M14; catalogue 410): three read from decodes of the time, an alphabetical code partly rebuilt

steps.what: All 17 images of M14 fetched through the DigitArq JSON backend. Telegrams on m0010-11, m0012-13, m0014-15, m0016 (m0017 is a telegram envelope).
First pass described m0014 as Paris -> Lisbon, 1910, 51 groups, and m0016 as Naples -> Lisbon.

Independent re-reading of the printed strips: m0014 runs Lisbon -> Paris, 13 May 1903 (stamp probable), 43 groups; m0016 runs Lisbon (Alcântara) -> Naples. The first pass's split into a 1903-04 and a 1910 code fails: Carlos and Sabugosa used different codes at the same time.
Transcribed the handwritten 1910 telegrams m0010 (16 groups) and m0012-13 (37 groups) with their headers; the word counts on the forms match.

Found the decodes of the time among the clear cards: m0009 (24-4-04) repeats m0016's clear opening and gives ten words for its ten groups; m0008 (21-5-10, 15 words for 16 groups) matches m0010; m0005 + m0004 (signed Sabugosa, with question marks at the receiver's circled groups) match m0012-13. Paired group by group.

The 52 values run in alphabetical order within each series (5-digit a-h, 4-digit i-v): grade C values have 3 of 406 and 0 of 136 pairs out of order; 2000 shuffles give at least 117 and 32. One-part code. The order also fixes the three-group spelling So/ver/al, puts the decoder's 'va' (0539) out of place, and puts 'assumpto' (13657) just after casar (13616).
Applied the 52 values to m0014 (1903, no decode): 6 of 43 groups have a value (diz, de x2, e x3); the others are bounded by their alphabetical neighbours only. Not enough to read.
One web search by the first pass: no printed decipherment of these telegrams. Not checked: biographies of Manuel II and studies of his 1910 marriage project.

outcome.method_basis: m0010, m0012-13 and m0016 are read from decodes of the time filed with them (m0008, m0005 + m0004, m0009); 52 code values were then tabulated by pairing groups with those decodes (an extension of the decipherments of the time, not cryptanalysis); m0014 (1903) has no decode and stays unread.

texts.label: m0010, London -> Lisbon, 21 May 1910
texts.summary: From London after Edward VII's funeral, Sabugosa tells Queen Amélie that the King intends to speak to the Queen so that Soveral, the Portuguese minister, can take up 'the matter' with her; news tomorrow.

texts.label: m0012-13, London -> Lisbon, received 24 May 1910
texts.summary: Queen Alexandra received Sabugosa with kind words; the King (George V) ended by saying he would see to getting him married; he has not seen the Princess; Soveral will handle the negotiation. The British marriage project for Manuel II in May 1910.

reading_review.note: Coherent except one phrase of the King's words, where the decoder's own query marks are kept as holes.

texts.label: m0016, Lisbon -> Naples, 24 Apr 1904
texts.summary: Sabugosa thanks the Queen, then at Naples, for a telegram that set his heart at rest, assures her of his constant loyalty, and is glad of good news.

reading_review.note: Clean; 'ser' for 'sou' is the code's infinitive, noted in the translation.

texts.label: m0014, Lisbon -> Paris, 13 May 1903
texts.summary: Duplicate copy ('ampliation') of a 52-word code telegram signed Sabugoso, to Paris, the day after King Carlos's telegram of 12 May 1903 (targets/carlos1903).
texts.note: 6 of 43 groups take a value from the other decodes (diz, de, e); not read.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 410). The catalogue dates the unit 1910; it also holds telegrams of 1903 and 1904. The decodes were not noticed in the first pass; they were found while checking the contact sheets for this pull request, and a reviewing agent re-read the decode cards and the 1910 groups against the images once more (it corrected 'Tratar é de' to 'tratar ei de', i.e. tratarei); the pairing is checked by the alphabetical order only. M14 also holds a decode of 22 May 1910 (m0001, probably continued on m0002) whose telegram is not in the file, and the Queen's clear reply of 21 May (m0007); both are transcribed in related_clear.md.

prior.where: Decodes of the time filed in the same unit: m0008 (for m0010), m0005 + m0004 (for m0012-13), m0009 (for m0016). No printed decipherment found (one web search); the 1910 marriage negotiations may be quoted from these cards in biographies of Manuel II, which were not checked.

human: WAINUT chose the catalogue items and set the rules; AI language-model agents fetched the images, transcribed, paired the decodes with the telegrams, and ran the order test. No hand correction of readings recorded.
